_comment_: P4-A: per-seat capacity map. Replaces the legacy single '4 Devin workers' cap with per-provider + per-model caps, a RAM governor, and a metered-seat class so subscription seats are exhausted before paid-per-token ones.
_comment_order: Expiry-first selection order (Nish, 2026-08-22): devin -> cursor -> cline -> free -> minimax (metered). Implemented in seat-lib.sh pick_seat; this file is data only.
_comment_ram_governor: ram_gb_per_worker=0.75 (2026-08-26). Measured LIVE worker RSS: mean 35 MB, total 0.07 GiB across running workers - the fleet's actual footprint is tiny. The previous 1.28 was the median of completed-unit MemoryPeak (n=14, p95 4.4 GB, max 4.8 GB), i.e. sized for the worst case. Sizing on typical is only safe BECAUSE the tail is now bounded three ways: per-worker MemoryHigh=3G throttles, RuntimeMaxSec=45min kills a wedge, and systemd-oomd kills at 80%/60s. Before those existed, the conservative number was correct. With ~10 GiB MemAvailable and the 2500 MB floor this yields ~10 lanes instead of 4, and the launch floor still recomputes every call so the ceiling falls automatically as memory is consumed. Re-derive from measurement, never edit by feel.
_comment_cursor_grok: cursor/cursor-grok-4.6-high: probe-and-exclude. One strike already (spawnSync ETIMEDOUT at 2026-08-25 00:47 IST). Probed twice after the strike and it responds healthy; cap held at 1 to limit blast radius. Raise to 2 if it stays clean for a week.
_comment_minimax: minimax direct (MiniMax-M3) classified as 'metered' per models.json cost field (input $0.30/M, output $1.20/M) even though the model name says 'Yearly Plus' — the cost field is the source of truth and 'Yearly Plus' is just a tier label. Selection order puts it LAST so subscription seats burn down first.
_comment_ollama_rule: ollama cap only covers deepseek-v4-flash:0731 — the DeepSeek-flash-only standing rule bans ollama/kimi-k2.7-code, ollama/deepseek-v4-pro:0813, and ollama/gpt-oss:20b. seat-lib.sh enumerate_seats() emits every model in models.json; the cap map here is the allowlist by being the only entries listed. (Code-level enforcement is a follow-up if the rule is ever loosened.)
_comment_cursor: cursor provider cap=1 (2026-08-25): cursor flakes with spawnSync ETIMEDOUT on long-running jobs; short probes are fine. The provider cap holds the fleet to one cursor worker at a time, and the code-level capable-provider whitelist in seat-lib.sh keeps cursor out of the heavy-task rotation. Raise to 2 if cursor stays clean on long jobs for a week.
_comment_devin: devin provider cap=4 (2026-08-25): devin hit its message rate limit at ~01:30 IST tonight. Auto-restart backoff in pi-issue@.service (Restart=on-failure, RestartSteps=3, ~6 min effective retry) handles the recovery, so the cap stays at 4. If rate-limit hits become daily, lower to 3.
_comment_seat_roster: Nish 2026-08-25: ALL seats available everywhere so work never stops. Ten seats probed live and answering: devin, cursor, cline, ollama (Ollama Cloud), minimax, commandcode, openrouter, grok (SuperGrok via grok-cli), zenmux, hetzner. zenmux and hetzner carry FREE lanes as well as credits, and openrouter has free lanes alongside credits - none of them are metered-only, so none is capped 0. Only providers with no working credential stay at 0.
_comment_credits: zenmux and openrouter both carry FREE lanes AND paid credits (Nish, 2026-08-25). class=metered records that, but seat-lib.sh computes class_of() and then ignores it - pick_seat buckets by literal provider name, so both currently sit in the FREE bucket and their credits can be spent as if free. free_providers_in_order is the only working control until that is fixed (fleet-ops#42): free lanes first, credit-bearing seats last.
_comment_grok: grok cap=0 (2026-08-26): SuperGrok's subscription covers the grok.com app and the grok CLI, NOT the x.ai API. pi reaching api.x.ai/v1 with the CLI's own OAuth token returns 403 'You have run out of credits or need a Grok subscription'. pi also has NO registered grok-cli adapter ('No API provider registered for api: grok-cli'), so the CLI route is not reachable from pi either. Raising this cap requires either x.ai API credits (money - Nish only) or a pi custom-provider extension wrapping the grok CLI. Tracked in fleet-ops#41.
